skill.name: backtesting-frameworks
skill.description: Build robust backtesting systems for trading strategies with proper handling of look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, and transaction costs. Use when developing trading algorithms, validating strategies, or building backtesting infrastructure.
skill.summary: Guides reliable trading backtests with bias controls, realistic costs, walk-forward testing, and robustness analysis.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Trading backtests often fail because they ignore bias, costs, and robustness checks. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design stronger research workflows.
actual_capabilities: Design event-driven backtesting structures with orders, fills, portfolios, and execution models.
Build vectorized backtests for simple strategies using shifted signals and trading costs.
Plan train, validation, test, and walk-forward evaluation workflows.
Model commissions, slippage, drawdowns, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, and related metrics.
Add Monte Carlo analysis to estimate drawdown risk and loss probabilities.
limitations: It does not provide live trading execution or broker integration.
It does not guarantee future performance or profitable strategies.
It depends on clean historical data supplied by the user.
It offers example patterns, not a complete maintained software package.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Strategy Backtest
use_cases.description: Create a testable backtest design with realistic assumptions, shifted signals, and clear performance metrics.

use_cases.title: Review Backtest Validity
use_cases.description: Check an existing research workflow for look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, overfitting, and missing costs.

use_cases.title: Plan Robustness Testing
use_cases.description: Add walk-forward splits and Monte Carlo analysis to measure strategy stability across market conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Backtest Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a basic backtest plan for this trading idea. Include data needs, assumptions, costs, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check for Bias
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my backtest design for look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, overfitting, and transaction cost gaps. List concrete fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Walk-Forward Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a walk-forward testing plan for this strategy. Define windows, parameter selection rules, metrics, and reporting outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test Research Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Monte Carlo and drawdown stress tests for these strategy returns. Explain what each result means and what limits remain.

output_examples.input: I have a moving average strategy and daily price data.
output_examples.output: A backtest plan with shifted signals, cost assumptions, train and test splits, and metrics for return, volatility, and drawdown.

output_examples.input: My strategy has a high Sharpe ratio on one data period.
output_examples.output: A review checklist covering overfitting risk, out-of-sample testing, parameter stability, transaction costs, and drawdown behavior.

output_examples.input: I need to explain whether results are robust.
output_examples.output: A robustness report outline with walk-forward results, Monte Carlo drawdown ranges, loss probabilities, and remaining data limitations.

best_practices: Define the hypothesis, universe, timeframe, and metrics before testing.
Use point-in-time data, realistic costs, and out-of-sample evaluation.
Report uncertainty with drawdowns, parameter stability, and Monte Carlo ranges.
anti_patterns: Optimizing parameters on the full history before reporting final results.
Ignoring delisted assets, market impact, commissions, or slippage.
Presenting backtest returns as financial advice or future guarantees.

faq.question: Does this skill execute trades?
faq.answer: No. It supports backtest design and research workflows, not live trading or broker execution.

faq.question: Can it help find look-ahead bias?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives checks for signal timing, point-in-time data, and train-test separation.

faq.question: Does it include transaction costs?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include commissions, slippage, and related cost modeling concepts.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompts can start with a simple strategy idea and build a structured plan.

faq.question: Does it replace financial judgment?
faq.answer: No. It helps evaluate research quality, but it does not provide investment advice.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in the skill metadata.
